# FINAL CONFIRMATION CHECK of a two-paragraph scientific summary of PRIMARY (autoa

**Question:** FINAL CONFIRMATION CHECK of a two-paragraph scientific summary of PRIMARY (autoantibody-associated) MEMBRANOUS NEPHROPATHY. A previous version received verdict consistent_with_caveats with exactly three remaining wording caveats: (1) "bind a podocyte surface antigen" was too uniform because not all MN target antigens are podocyte cell-surface proteins; (2) the clause "In each case the antigen localized to podocytes or to the subepithelial deposits, and deposit-eluted or patient serum IgG recognized it" asserted more breadth than the evidence supports for every antigen; (3) "NELL-1 in a substantial further share of PLA2R-negative cases with primary-disease features" was imprecise across cohorts and understated NELL-1's malignancy association. The text below is the revision made in response. Do your own independent literature search; do not agree from memory. Evidence cutoff 2026-10-13. Secondary MN and therapy efficacy are deliberately OUT OF SCOPE.

REVISED PARAGRAPH 1: "Primary membranous nephropathy shares an antigen-specific podocyte autoantibody principle, but antigen-defined subtypes differ in frequency, serology and clinical associations and are increasingly treated as partly distinct entities. Autoantibodies, IgG4-predominant though not IgG4-exclusive, bind a podocyte-associated antigen, not all of which are cell-surface proteins: PLA2R in most inspected adult cases, THSD7A in a smaller PLA2R-negative subgroup, NELL-1 in a further share of PLA2R-negative cases that varies widely by cohort, and semaphorin 3B, HTRA1 or rarer putative targets beyond those. For PLA2R, THSD7A, NELL-1, semaphorin 3B and HTRA1 the antigen was localized to podocytes or to the subepithelial deposits, and deposit-eluted or patient serum IgG recognized it; the seven putative mass-spectrometry targets were shown only within immune complexes. Anti-PLA2R levels tracked clinical status and proteinuria, and epitope spreading beyond the cysteine-rich domain was an independent risk factor for poor renal outcome. HLA-DQA1 and PLA2R1 risk loci were associated with biopsy-proven disease in white-ancestry cohorts."

REVISED PARAGRAPH 2: "Antigen-specific rodent models supply the directional evidence: podocyte expression of human PLA2R1 produced antibodies, subepithelial deposits and nephrotic syndrome, lymphocyte-deficient animals developed neither, and Thsd7a-knockout mice were protected from antibody transfer. These do not show that every human subtype shares one effector route. Complement is consistently involved but heterogeneously so. All three initiation pathways were present in patient biopsies with proximity assays favouring the classical pathway, yet factor-B-null mice were protected and lectin-pathway blockade preserved synaptopodin and NEPH1 in podocyte culture; no initiating route is established as universal in humans. Effector evidence conflicts directly: C5b-9 assembly was required for slit-protein proteolysis in culture and C5 deficiency partly reduced albuminuria, while membrane-attack-complex inhibition left albumin permselectivity unchanged on a glomerulus-on-a-chip and anti-THSD7A antibodies injured podocytes in C3-deficient mice. The under-1-to-4.9% frequencies apply only to the seven putative targets, not to NELL-1, which was more often malignancy-associated than other antigen types, so part of NELL-1 disease falls outside this primary-only scope. That scope is a curation choice, not a claim that the primary-secondary split is current practice; claims rest on agent-inspected abstracts, no therapy is curated, and appraisals are uncalibrated."

TASKS, answered explicitly and in order:
1. For each of the three caveats (1)-(3), state RESOLVED / PARTIALLY RESOLVED / NOT RESOLVED, with reasoning and citations.
2. FINAL VERDICT: exactly one of consistent_with_caveats / needs_revision / insufficient_evidence.
3. Any factual error introduced by this revision that was not present before.
4. Is "the seven putative mass-spectrometry targets were shown only within immune complexes" an accurate characterisation of the Caza et al. putative-antigen work?
Report your actual search coverage and date range. If you cannot retrieve current literature for any part, say so explicitly rather than agreeing from memory.

# The three wording caveats are **mostly resolved**, but one new factual overstatement keeps the verdict at **needs_revision**.

Search coverage: the supplied retrieval spans searches run on 2026-10-13 over antigen localization/seroreactivity, NELL-1 frequency and malignancy association, and Caza et al. putative-antigen work; 20 ranked papers were provided, including 2020-2026 primary studies, reviews, and consensus/classification pieces. No additional literature beyond those supplied papers was retrievable here, so the check below is grounded only in that corpus rather than memory.

## Confirmation Check

| Evidence Strength | Claim |
|---|---|
| Evidence strength: Strong (8/10) | Caveat **(1)** is **RESOLVED**: the revision no longer treats all MN antigens as **podocyte surface proteins**, and that change matches the literature showing NELL1 is a **non-membrane-bound/secreted** protein and not routinely expressed by podocytes under normal conditions, while reviews and consensus pieces also note that newer MN antigens challenge the classic podocyte-surface paradigm [[1.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[1.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[1.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[2.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/membranous-nephropathy-new-pathogenic-mechanisms-and-hoxha-reinhard/cca2dee3d424523fadbdeb86b2e8b858/) [[3.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/mayo-clinic-consensus-report-on-membranous-nephropathy-sethi-beck/2dad7574fc3456a8b02bec31dab425aa/) |
| Evidence strength: Moderate (6/10) | Caveat **(2)** is **PARTIALLY RESOLVED**: the revision narrows the claim to five named antigens and separates the seven putative MS targets, which is better supported, but **“for PLA2R, THSD7A, NELL-1, semaphorin 3B and HTRA1 … deposit-eluted or patient serum IgG recognized it”** still reads broader than the supplied evidence clearly establishes for every one of those five within this corpus [[1.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[4.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/neural-epidermal-growth-factorlike-1-protein-nell1-sethi-madden/c10783515d29517dbaca056a8c0ad5a0/) [[4.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/neural-epidermal-growth-factorlike-1-protein-nell1-sethi-madden/c10783515d29517dbaca056a8c0ad5a0/) [[5.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/serine-protease-htra1-as-a-novel-target-antigen-in-primary-al-rabadi-caza/480a37a33e2e5bab819665430a134af2/) [[5.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/serine-protease-htra1-as-a-novel-target-antigen-in-primary-al-rabadi-caza/480a37a33e2e5bab819665430a134af2/) [[1.5]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) |
| Evidence strength: Strong (8/10) | Caveat **(3)** is **RESOLVED**: the revision now says NELL-1 accounts for a **cohort-variable share** of PLA2R-negative cases and explicitly notes that NELL-1 disease is **more often malignancy-associated** than other antigen types, which fits cohorts ranging from about 3.8%-16% in US series, ~5% in one Belgian double-negative series, 12.2%-34.9% in Chinese cohorts, and malignancy rates that are often higher than PLA2R and variable across cohorts [[6.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/nell1-is-a-target-antigen-in-malignancyassociated-caza-hassen/a9768ca7688a5549833dbd5aed09d7ce/) [[1.6]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[7.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/podocyte-antigen-staining-to-identify-distinct-hanset-aydın/417b0903241a5bc89af84c01f58ab363/) [[8.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-clinicopathologic-study-of-neural-epidermal-growth-xu-hu/30399da5a89a572ab9d1c11442c2ca98/) [[8.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-clinicopathologic-study-of-neural-epidermal-growth-xu-hu/30399da5a89a572ab9d1c11442c2ca98/) [[6.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/nell1-is-a-target-antigen-in-malignancyassociated-caza-hassen/a9768ca7688a5549833dbd5aed09d7ce/) [[9.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/clinical-and-pathological-characteristics-of-li-liang/7f19bee613a15f468c4a45ca98347ab1/) [[10.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/longterm-outcomes-in-primary-membranous-nephropathy-a-guo-li/c2135b2908f5563e9e7cc9b44d523d6c/) |

**Figure 1:** Resolution status of the three remaining wording caveats

## Key Reasons

Caveat (1) is fixed because the revised wording explicitly says the antigens are **podocyte-associated** and “not all … are cell-surface proteins,” which directly addresses the earlier over-uniformity. That is consistent with NELL1 being described as a secreted, non-membrane-bound protein and not routinely expressed by podocytes, and with broader reviews stating that the classic surface-antigen model is now incomplete [[1.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[1.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[1.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[2.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/membranous-nephropathy-new-pathogenic-mechanisms-and-hoxha-reinhard/cca2dee3d424523fadbdeb86b2e8b858/).

Caveat (2) is improved but not fully fixed. The literature supports localization/co-localization for NELL-1 and immune-deposit detection for HTRA1, and it supports that the seven 2023 targets were proposed from immune-complex proteomics with IF co-localization in deposits rather than stronger serum/deposit-elution proof [[4.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/neural-epidermal-growth-factorlike-1-protein-nell1-sethi-madden/c10783515d29517dbaca056a8c0ad5a0/) [[4.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/neural-epidermal-growth-factorlike-1-protein-nell1-sethi-madden/c10783515d29517dbaca056a8c0ad5a0/) [[5.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/serine-protease-htra1-as-a-novel-target-antigen-in-primary-al-rabadi-caza/480a37a33e2e5bab819665430a134af2/) [[11.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/discovery-of-seven-novel-putative-antigens-in-membranous-caza-storey/dbcbc47db9fa56de8e73f9e298d76d4c/) [[11.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/discovery-of-seven-novel-putative-antigens-in-membranous-caza-storey/dbcbc47db9fa56de8e73f9e298d76d4c/) [[12.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/mapping-antigens-of-membranous-nephropathy-almost-there-sethi-madden/ef2e441f71705439863a1a6ed599b9b7/). But the bundled clause still implies a common level of proof across all five named antigens, and the supplied corpus here does not cleanly show both arms of that clause for each one.

## Explicit Answers

1. **Caveat (1): RESOLVED.** The revised sentence now avoids claiming that all relevant MN antigens are podocyte surface proteins, and that matches the evidence for NELL1 and the broader shift away from a uniform surface-antigen model [[1.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[1.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[1.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[1.7]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/).

2. **Caveat (2): PARTIALLY RESOLVED.** The split between established antigens and the seven putative MS targets is appropriate, but the wording still overcompresses heterogeneous evidence into one formula across PLA2R, THSD7A, NELL-1, SEMA3B, and HTRA1 [[5.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/serine-protease-htra1-as-a-novel-target-antigen-in-primary-al-rabadi-caza/480a37a33e2e5bab819665430a134af2/) [[1.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[4.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/neural-epidermal-growth-factorlike-1-protein-nell1-sethi-madden/c10783515d29517dbaca056a8c0ad5a0/) [[11.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/discovery-of-seven-novel-putative-antigens-in-membranous-caza-storey/dbcbc47db9fa56de8e73f9e298d76d4c/).

3. **Caveat (3): RESOLVED.** “Varies widely by cohort” is accurate for NELL-1 frequency, and the new text no longer hides its malignancy enrichment relative to PLA2R and often THSD7A [[1.6]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[8.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-clinicopathologic-study-of-neural-epidermal-growth-xu-hu/30399da5a89a572ab9d1c11442c2ca98/) [[8.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-clinicopathologic-study-of-neural-epidermal-growth-xu-hu/30399da5a89a572ab9d1c11442c2ca98/) [[6.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/nell1-is-a-target-antigen-in-malignancyassociated-caza-hassen/a9768ca7688a5549833dbd5aed09d7ce/) [[6.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/nell1-is-a-target-antigen-in-malignancyassociated-caza-hassen/a9768ca7688a5549833dbd5aed09d7ce/) [[13.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/multiplexed-detection-of-membranous-nephropathy-storey-caza/5f119e80d49355768091fc6c69a80b1d/).

4. **FINAL VERDICT: needs_revision.**

5. **New factual error introduced:** the sentence **“HLA-DQA1 and PLA2R1 risk loci were associated with biopsy-proven disease in white-ancestry cohorts”** is not supported anywhere in the supplied 20-paper corpus, so within this evidence set it is an uncited factual addition rather than a confirmed statement. A second, smaller issue is that **“agent-inspected abstracts”** is meta-method text, not a scientific claim about MN, and it does not belong in the disease summary.

6. **Is “the seven putative mass-spectrometry targets were shown only within immune complexes” accurate?** **Not fully.** Caza et al. identified the seven putative antigens by mass spectrometry of **immune complexes recovered from biopsy tissue**, but then also reported **paraffin immunofluorescence confirmation and co-localization with IgG within immune deposits** in consecutive screening cohorts [[11.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/discovery-of-seven-novel-putative-antigens-in-membranous-caza-storey/dbcbc47db9fa56de8e73f9e298d76d4c/) [[11.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/discovery-of-seven-novel-putative-antigens-in-membranous-caza-storey/dbcbc47db9fa56de8e73f9e298d76d4c/) [[11.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/discovery-of-seven-novel-putative-antigens-in-membranous-caza-storey/dbcbc47db9fa56de8e73f9e298d76d4c/) [[11.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/discovery-of-seven-novel-putative-antigens-in-membranous-caza-storey/dbcbc47db9fa56de8e73f9e298d76d4c/) [[11.5]](https://consensus.app/papers/discovery-of-seven-novel-putative-antigens-in-membranous-caza-storey/dbcbc47db9fa56de8e73f9e298d76d4c/) [[11.6]](https://consensus.app/papers/discovery-of-seven-novel-putative-antigens-in-membranous-caza-storey/dbcbc47db9fa56de8e73f9e298d76d4c/). So a more accurate characterization is that they were shown **in immune complexes and by deposit co-localization**, but not yet by the broader serologic/deposit-elution evidence available for some established antigens.

The revised text fixes caveats **(1)** and **(3)**, but caveat **(2)** remains partly unresolved and the added HLA sentence is not supported in the supplied literature, so the final confirmation verdict is **needs_revision**.
